title: Yama's thumb-sized person in the heart
hookLine: Death tells Nachiketa of a person the size of a thumb in the heart; the sutras say it's Brahman.
carry: the one in your heart is brahman itself
tomorrow: where does the world come from: a potter, or the clay?
last: RITES READY THE MIND. KNOWING FREES.

lines: A PERSON THE SIZE OF A THUMB.
cards: A hand laid flat on the chest finds it right away: a steady knock, keeping time. In the Katha Upanishad, Death himself, Yama, is teaching a boy named Nachiketa, who turned down every other gift for the truth about death.
And Yama gives that spot a stranger measurement. A person the size of a thumb, he says, stands in the middle of the body. Lord of what was and what will be.
Like a flame without smoke. Read quickly, it sounds like a tiny being behind the ribs. The Brahma Sutras stop at this line and ask something plain.
Who is this, exactly? A small soul, or Brahman itself?

teach.b: The sutra answers from the words themselves. Look at the title the Upanishad gives: lord of past and future. A soul caught in one life doesn't rule what was and what will be.
That title belongs to Brahman. So, the sutra says, the thumb-sized one is Brahman. Then why so small?

teach.h: THE MEASURE BELONGS TO THE HEART.
teach.b: The next sutra gives the reason, and Shankara opens it up: the measure belongs to the heart. Brahman is spoken of as thumb-sized because that's where the text points the seeker to find it, in the space of the heart.
Shankara reaches for an everyday picture.

teach.h: SPACE IN A REED IS STILL SPACE.
teach.b: The space inside a hollow reed takes the reed's measure. It's still just space, as wide as all the rest. That's how jnana reads here.
It doesn't add a tiny creature to the chest. It recognizes the boundless where it's met. And the Upanishad says one more thing about that person: it's the same today and tomorrow.
The flame doesn't flicker with the days. This is one of Hinduism's best-loved teachings: God isn't only far away.

teach.h: THE LORD DWELLS IN THE HEART.
teach.b: The Bhagavad Gita says it near its end: the Lord dwells in the heart of all beings. Shankara's reading goes all the way.

teach.h: THE BOUNDLESS, MET IN THE HEART.
teach.b: The one in your heart is Brahman itself. Other Vedanta teachers read these sutras in their own way; here we're following Shankara.

how: In Advaita Vedanta, the thumb-sized person of the Katha Upanishad is read as Brahman pointed out in the heart, and some teachers use the space of the heart as a place to turn attention during meditation.

o: a skill for measuring the parts of the soul
knowledge that sees the boundless where it's met
a vision of a tiny being living in the body

games.q: the thumb-sized person. tap the pairs.
p: a person the size of a thumb
a title that belongs to Brahman
the measure belongs to the heart
takes its shape, still just space

s: the Upanishad means a tiny being literally lives in the chest
the sutras read the thumb-sized one as Brahman; the measure belongs to the heart, where it's sought.
the sutra decides who the thumb-sized one is from the title the text gives it
lord of past and future: a title that belongs to Brahman, not to a soul in one life.
the Upanishad says that person changes from day to day
it says the same today and tomorrow, like a flame without smoke.

games.q: a friend reads the Katha line and says: so a tiny soul lives behind my ribs. you're Shankara. what do you say?
o: it's Brahman, spoken of as small because the heart is where it's sought.
yes: a separate small person lives there, ruling the body.
it's only a poem about courage, with nothing to know in it.
games.why: The title 'lord of past and future' shows it's Brahman; the thumb's measure belongs to the heart, like space taking a reed's shape.

practice: Lay one hand flat on the middle of your chest and feel it rise and fall. Notice the heartbeat under your palm, if you can find it, and the warmth where hand meets shirt.
Then widen your attention to the space of the whole room, and notice that the space inside the chest and the space outside aren't two different kinds.
If you pray, you can rest there with the one the text calls lord of past and future; if not, just rest in the width.

wordCard.voice: Jnana: knowledge that frees. Here, it reads a thumb-sized person in the heart as Brahman, met where the seeker looks.

orig.note: Sanskrit angushthamatra, the measure of a thumb; the Katha Upanishad's phrase for the person in the middle of the body.

carryVoice: Your line, from Yama to Nachiketa: the one in your heart is Brahman itself. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Katha Upanishad 4.12–13 (2.1.12–13): the person the size of a thumb in the middle of the body, lord of past and future, like a light without smoke, the same today and tomorrow
Brahma Sutra 1.3.24–25 with Shankara's commentary (the thumb-sized one is the Lord, from the word 'lord'; the measure is relative to the heart)
Katha Upanishad 1.1.20–29 (Nachiketa asks Yama what happens after death and turns down every other gift)
Bhagavad Gita 18.61 (the Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, Arjuna)
